rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child. Both are presidential messages concerning a foreign natural disaster, express the sentiment of the United States Government and people, and describe American relief assistance as intended to alleviate the affected population's suffering. The child's compact formulation closely condenses C03's distinctive combination of national sympathy, government-and-people attribution, and gratification concerning U.S. assistance. C17 and C10 share relief-related language but are appreciations addressed to relief participants rather than sympathy messages to a foreign president.

shared_material.child_excerpt: in the name of the Government and the people of the United States our deep sympathy for the suffering caused to so many of the Italian people
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a contribution from the government and the people of the United States and an indication of our solidarity and desire to alleviate in part the distress of the Mexican people during this time of suffering
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel attribution to the U.S. Government and people, coupled with sympathy for a foreign population suffering from a natural disaster.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whatever assistance United States forces, stationed in Italy, may have been able to provide to alleviate this suffering is a matter of gratification to me and to the American people.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It afforded our two peoples another opportunity to demonstrate to each other and to the world the brotherly bonds that exist between your great country and my own... relief operations... desire to alleviate in part the distress of the Mexican people
shared_material.explanation: Both messages connect U.S. disaster-relief operations with alleviating suffering and present that aid as an expression of solidarity between the two peoples.
